description:
About Our Team – SKYNETICS 🚀

We are SKYNETICS, a passionate and enthusiastic team of six members driven by curiosity, creativity, innovation, and a shared interest in space science and technology.

Our goal is to explore challenging problems, transform creative ideas into practical solutions, and contribute to the future of space exploration. We are particularly interested in astronomy, space technology, scientific research, artificial intelligence, software development, and STEM education.
summary:
1. What we developed
Team Skynetics built Orbit Academy, a free, browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for ages 8 to 14. Cadets play short 3-5 minute missions across five modules: Body in Space, Suit Up & Spacewalk, Mission Control Comms, Systems Check, and Launch, Orbit & Landing. A Moon Mission capstone, inspired by NASA's Artemis program, combines all five skills. Cadets earn XP and badges and rise from Cadet to Commander. It runs on any phone, tablet or laptop, works offline, needs no account, and opens each mission with credited NASA imagery.

2. How it addresses the challenge
The challenge asks for a trainer that lets juniors experience astronaut preparation. Each module is a hands-on simulation based on real training areas, such as pool-based spacewalk practice and daily crew exercise. Scoring rewards safety above speed, as in real spaceflight, and difficulty adapts to each cadet. Skill meters for safety, technical knowledge, teamwork and fitness show teachers what a student actually learned.

3. Why it is important
Children see launches, not the years of training behind them, and most space content is passive. Orbit Academy turns inspiration into practice, building problem-solving, teamwork and STEM interest early. Being offline-capable, account-free and ad-free, it reaches classrooms with limited bandwidth and keeps children's data on the device, helping widen the pipeline of future scientists, engineers and astronauts.
details:
Orbit Academy is a free, browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for ages 8 to 14. Cadets play short missions based on real astronaut training, earn XP and badges, and rise from Cadet to Commander. The demo has three playable missions: Suit Up (put the spacesuit checklist in order), Systems Check (keep oxygen, power, water and temperature in range), and Orbit Sandbox (choose a launch speed and see whether you re-enter, orbit or escape).

Benefits: learners practise decisions instead of just watching videos, safety counts more than speed, and it needs no account, ads or install. Progress stays on the child’s device.

Impact: turn children’s curiosity about space into hands-on practice, build problem-solving and teamwork, and widen the pipeline of future STEM careers, including in classrooms with limited internet.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the Canvas API, localStorage, and NASA Image and Video Library imagery. No special hardware is needed, and Claude helped produce the code and documents.

Creativity: real training turned into 3-5 minute games, a real gravity calculation in the orbit mission, and a rank ladder with badges.

Factors considered: age-appropriateness, offline access, privacy, scientific accuracy, accessibility and a small hackathon-sized scope. Adaptive difficulty and teacher dashboards are planned.
